identity: A page from a UAE school Islamic-Education (al-tarbiya al-islamiyya) textbook: the lesson 'al-Iqtida bi-Rasul Allah' on Surat al-Ahzab 21-27. It is not running prose but a laid-out pedagogical page whose visual blocks have been flattened by OCR: a title banner with its verse reference, a first-person learning-objectives list, rubric headings ('abadir li-attaallam', 'astakhdim maharati li-attaallam', 'ataammal wa-astanbit', 'taqyim al-nataij', 'al-sidq suluk wa-amal'), activity prompts, a two-column vocabulary gloss table, expository tafsir paragraphs, four cited hadiths, and a closing values sidebar on al-sidq. The token Q is a placeholder standing in for an excised Quranic quotation block.
law: A sentence here is one complete discourse unit, not one clause. Three unit types coexist. (a) Display units - title, verse reference, rubric heading, table cell or gloss, quoted verse block - each closes a unit even with no verb, because the following stretch cannot syntactically continue it. (b) First-person objective and activity items (asmau, afassiru, astantiju, ahaddidu, urattibu, ubayyinu...) - one item, one unit. (c) Expository sentences, which in this register run long (an uncontested 31-token sentence sits at 118-148) and are held together by wa- and fa- coordination, hal accusatives and relative chains. So I cut on change of discourse type, and on a genuinely new predication with a new subject. I do NOT cut on fa- resultative linkage, on wa- coordinating two predicates of one topic, or before an attached source citation (sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Hibban, Al Imran), which belongs to the segment it documents. The <NL> paragraphing is demonstrably lossy - one block runs 379 tokens and swallows headings whole - so paragraph structure confirms boundaries but never bounds them.
reasoning: [i2] The title 'al-Iqtida bi-Rasul Allah' and the reference 'Surat al-Ahzab 27 21' cannot form one phrase - no idafa, no apposition - so they are two display units; marked lo only because a header banner may have been a single typeset line. [i88, i91, i95, i96] The 21-token block at 80-100 is four flattened elements: the prediction prompt ending 'malakan', the rubric heading 'astakhdim maharati li-attaallam', the instruction 'atlu wa-ahfaz Surat al-Ahzab', then the verse block Q. I separate 95 from 96 because here Q is governed by nothing, unlike 'qala Allah Q Al Imran' at 164 and 'fa-qala Q' at 594, where Q is the object of a verb of saying and stays inline; that contrast is the whole argument, and it is why 95 is lo while 96 is hi - 96 holds under either analysis, since 'ataarraf tafsir al-mufradat al-quraniyya' is a new heading. [i103, i110] Table debris: 'al-mufrada tafsiruha' is the header row, 'wa-fa ahdihi' and 'husunuhum' are glosses (of nahbahu and sayasiyahum), and 'afham dalalat al-ayat' is the next section heading. 110 is the surer of the two because a heading visibly begins there; 103 is lo. I did not cut between 'al-mufrada' and 'tafsiruha' - that is cell-level, below sentence grain. [i161] Asyndetic 'qala Allah' after the complete predication ending 'fi jami al-ahwal' is a period site in this register. The apparent counter-example at 593 uses fa-qala, which binds, so the two sites do not conflict. [i232] 'wa-minhum man baqiya hayyan ... wa-lam yukhlif wadahu' closes the second of the paired groups and is a 17-token mirror of the 12-token 'fa-min haulai ... fa-stushhidu fi sabilihi' that got its own paragraph at 203-214. I left 'bi-khilaf al-munafiqin' (255) attached: bi-khilaf is a preposition and reads as a contrastive adjunct, not a sentence opener. [i266, i268] The narrative ends at 'adbarahum'; 'ataammal wa-astanbit' is a rubric heading of exactly the shape that stands alone as its own paragraph elsewhere in this same document ('abadir li-attaallam', 46-47). That internal parallel is strong, so both cuts are hi. By the same test I did NOT cut after 'urattib wa-asnif' (547): there the following words are its direct object, not a fresh clause. [i343] 'a-tasna hadha wa-qad jaaka min Allah an qad ghufira lak ma taqaddama min dhanbik wa-ma taakhkhar' is a question and carries a question mark; the answer 'qala a-fala akunu abdan shakuran' opens the next unit. Source tags stay attached throughout (298, 311, 351, 360). [i389-i451] The tafsir chain after 'taqyim al-nataij' is fa- and wa- welded. I cut where a new predication with a new subject starts - 'wa-amma man waada' (390), 'wa-hadha min bab' (407), 'wa-hadha yahfaz' (418), the imperative 'fa-nzur' (433) - and kept 'fa-huwa yafalu ma yurid' and 'fa-la yanshaghil ahad' welded to their causes. The 417/432 pair is my weakest stretch: the two wa-hadha clauses could equally be one comma-joined sentence, hence lo on 417. [i485, i499, i527] The three-way amma / wa-amma / wa-amma chain on the believers, the polytheists and Banu Qurayza is read as three sentences rather than one, because each branch runs 14-28 tokens. Inside the last branch I cut at 'iqab' (527) rather than at 'amwalahum' (533): the amma-clause about Banu Qurayza closes there, and 'fa-awratha Allah al-muminin' shifts the topic to what the believers gained. Marked lo - 46 tokens unsplit would be long, but the document's longest defensible single sentence is 31. [i584] I cut at this wa-qad site but not at the parallel one at 198 ('wa-qad bayyanat al-ayat fadlahum'), on a stated rule: cut at wa-qad only when the following clause is substantial and introduces a new subject. At 198 the remainder is 4 tokens and stays attached; at 585 it is 10 tokens with Allah as a new subject. Still marked lo, since the rule is my own and untested. [i633] 'maa man yasduq al-insan' is a question heading and 'al-sidq maa Allah awwalan wa-yakunu bi-l-yaqin ...' is its answer; I did not cut after 'awwalan' because the following wa-yakunu coordinates inside the answer. Deliberately left whole: 49-78 (30t, one bada an ... dhakara sentence with trailing relative and hal chains), 118-148 (31t, single verb daat with cascading circumstantial accusatives), 168-188 (21t), 190-201 (12t, fa-ma ... illa focus construction plus a 4-token wa-qad tail), 216-232 vs 233-266 boundary aside, and 596-611 (16t; 'thumma innahu' would normally open a sentence, but only 6 tokens precede it, too short to stand alone here).
